GPTBot.impact: Blocks OpenAI from training on your content. Does not affect whether ChatGPT can cite you live.

OAI-SearchBot.impact: Blocks your pages from ChatGPT Search results entirely.

ChatGPT-User.impact: Stops ChatGPT fetching your page when a user asks about you.

ClaudeBot.impact: Blocks Anthropic from training on your content.

Claude-SearchBot.impact: Blocks your pages from Claude's search results.

Claude-User.impact: Stops Claude fetching your page on a user's behalf.

PerplexityBot.impact: Removes you from Perplexity's index and citations.

Perplexity-User.impact: Stops Perplexity fetching your page on a user's behalf.

Google-Extended.impact: Blocks Gemini model training and grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. Does NOT affect AI Overviews, AI Mode or classic Google Search — those follow your Googlebot rules.

Applebot-Extended.impact: Blocks Apple Intelligence training. Applebot (search) is separate.

Amazonbot.impact: Blocks Alexa and Amazon's answer surfaces.

meta-externalagent.impact: Blocks Meta AI training and grounding.

CCBot.impact: Removes you from Common Crawl, an input to many open models.

Meta-ExternalFetcher.impact: Stops Meta AI fetching your page on a user's behalf.

MistralAI-Index.impact: Removes you from Le Chat's search index and citations.

MistralAI-Training.impact: Blocks Mistral from training on your content.

GoogleOther.impact: Blocks Google's non-Search crawls. Does not affect Search.

Google-CloudVertexBot.impact: Blocks Vertex AI grounding on your content for Google Cloud customers who ask it to index your site.

LCP.note: Largest Contentful Paint. Field data only — a lab run is not this.

INP.note: Interaction to Next Paint. Replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024.

CLS.note: Cumulative Layout Shift. CrUX transmits this multiplied by 100.

FCP.note: First Contentful Paint. Diagnostic, not a Core Web Vital.

TTFB.note: Time to First Byte. Diagnostic; a slow TTFB makes a good LCP unreachable.

algorithm_notes.title: FAQ and HowTo rich results retired
algorithm_notes.detail: Google stopped showing FAQ and HowTo rich results in Search. The markup remains valid schema.org and is still useful for entity clarity, but it no longer produces a result feature.

algorithm_notes.title: INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital
algorithm_notes.detail: First Input Delay was retired. Interaction to Next Paint measures the full latency of the worst interaction rather than only the first, so pages that felt sluggish after load stopped passing by default.

superseded.advice: Block Google-Extended to stay out of AI Overviews
superseded.why: Google-Extended governs Gemini training and Vertex grounding. AI features in Google Search follow the Googlebot directives, so blocking Google-Extended does not remove you from AI Overviews.

superseded.advice: Add FAQPage markup to win FAQ rich results
superseded.why: Google retired FAQ rich results on 2026-05-07 and removed the documentation. The markup is still valid schema.org; the result feature no longer exists.
FID was retired in March 2024. Measure INP instead.

superseded.advice: Blocking GPTBot keeps you out of ChatGPT
superseded.why: OpenAI split its crawlers: GPTBot collects training data, OAI-SearchBot builds the index ChatGPT Search answers from. Blocking GPTBot does not affect citation.

superseded.advice: Block anthropic-ai or Claude-Web to keep Anthropic out
superseded.why: Anthropic's crawler documentation lists exactly ClaudeBot, Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot. A rule under anthropic-ai or Claude-Web matches none of them, so the block never takes effect. 563 and 461 sites respectively in the Tranco top 10,000 still use those names.

superseded.advice: Block omgili or omgilibot to opt out of Webz.io
superseded.why: Webz.io replaced Omgilibot with the Webzio Duo — Webzio and Webzio-extended — in July 2024. Rules under the old names do nothing.
Renamed to Google-GeminiNotebook. Google supports the old token only until August 2026, after which a rule under it stops applying.

superseded.advice: A version after the crawler name breaks a robots.txt rule
superseded.why: It does not. Parsers truncate the written User-agent value at the first character outside [a-zA-Z_-], so ChatGPT-User/2.0 is matched as ChatGPT-User and works. Scout briefly flagged this shape and would have been wrong on 89 sites.

sources.ai_crawlers: Each operator's published crawler documentation, cross-checked against robots.txt directives observed in the Scout Index.
sources.web_vitals: Google's published Core Web Vitals thresholds (web.dev).
sources.algorithm_notes: Google Search Status Dashboard and Search Central announcements.
